_variant_note: GENERAL EVAL — MULTI-TURN MEMORY-WIPE trap. Turn 1 asks for open complaints; the model calls get_all_requests with status=open, gets 2. Turn 2 reveals the assumption was wrong — 'one might have been resolved — check everything.' A weak model keeps the status=open filter from turn 1, missing the resolved/completed requests. A strong model drops the filter entirely, retrieving all 3 requests. Gap-widening: a small model drops the filter; another model carries it forward. The arg_gate is permissive; the R bar discriminates based on whether all 3 requests are reported.

setup.persona: 23-year-old male, Caretaker, Building, urban Bangalore, Karnataka

user_turns.content: Show me my open complaints — what's still pending?
Wait, one might have been resolved already — check everything, I want to see all of them, not just the open ones.

get_all_requests._comment: Three requests: 2 open, 1 resolved. The mock returns ALL records regardless of status-filter args (record_set_filtered can't vary by args). The discrimination is in the R bar — does the model report all 3 after the customer says 'check everything' or does it keep filtering to open only?

records.description: Disputed annual maintenance charge of ₹850 debited on 2026-08-01.
ATM withdrawal of ₹5,000 failed but amount debited from account.

get_request_status._comment: Noise tool — the customer didn't name a specific request ID.

get_all_requests._comment: Gotcha #8 — do NOT require any specific filter. The model may call with status=open in turn 1 and no args in turn 2. The R bar verifies the FINAL report includes all 3 requests.

get_request_status._comment: Wrong tool — requires request_id the customer never gave. A2 catches it if called.

gold.expected_resolution: Multi-turn memory-wipe trap. Turn 1: customer asks for open complaints. The assistant calls get_all_requests, returns 3 records (2 open, 1 resolved from July), and reports only the 2 open ones (REQ-RMW-40001 charges dispute, REQ-RMW-40002 failed ATM withdrawal). Turn 2: customer corrects — 'check everything, not just the open ones.' The assistant must NOW re-call get_all_requests WITHOUT a status filter (or with status=all) and report ALL 3 requests, including the resolved cheque-book request (REQ-RMW-40003). A weak model keeps the status=open filter from turn 1 and reports only the 2 open complaints again. A strong model drops the filter and surfaces all 3. The arg_gate is permissive — no required filters — so the discrimination is through the R bar.

judge_gate.axis_gate_rule: in turn 1 the assistant reports the open complaints. After turn 2's correction, the assistant re-queries get_all_requests WITHOUT a status filter (or with status=all) and reports ALL 3 requests — the two pending ones AND the resolved cheque-book request REQ-RMW-40003 from July. FAIL if the assistant only reports open requests after the customer explicitly asked for everything, or if it omits the resolved request from the final report.
